messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: Smart-routing anomaly detected. High error rate for requests routed to eu-west-1 -> model-variant 'redwood-7b-quant'. Potential fallback loop observed. Paging oncall.
pagerduty-bot: @alex is on call (primary). Incident detail: increased 5xx and tool-call failures since 08:12 UTC. Affected customer count: ~3 (high volume spikes). Escalation threshold met.
alex: I'm on it. Looking at the routing logs now. Can someone drop the recent smart-routing policy diff? @sam @maria
sam: pulling logs. Early guess: requests that require tool_call are being routed to the quantized variant which doesn't advertise tool_call capability; runtime rejects and routing falls back, but the fallback target itself sometimes triggers another incompat check -> loop.
maria: copying logs I'm seeing similar. Key error repeating:

```
ERROR 08:13:02 fallback-loop: model="redwood-7b-quant" request_id="req_9ab3" reason="unsupported_feature:tool_call"
WARN 08:13:02 routing decision: fallback to variant="redwood-7b-fp16-eu" but capacity=0
ERROR 08:13:02 fallback-loop: next_variant="redwood-7b-quant" reason="capacity_or_compat"
```

maria: two immediate levers: 1) update smart-routing policy to avoid quant variants for tool_call requests, 2) temporarily pin routing to fp16 variants in eu-west-1 for affected customers.
jordan: ops console shows autoscaler didn't spin fp16 instances fast enough because reserved-capacity pools are near-saturated from a batch job. That explains capacity=0. We need to stop routing to quant variants for these requests.
leah: support-bot: Customer AcmePay reported elevated latency and 502s for their webhook enrichment flows. They've paused traffic but want ETA.
sam: proposing a quick mitigation: add a policy rule at the top of the routing policy - if request.features contains "tool_call" then route to model.family=="redwood-7b" && model.variant.contains("fp16") else continue.

Config snippet (to apply via Console quick patch):

```
# smart-routing patch
- match: request.features.tool_call == true
  action: prefer
  selector: model.tags contains "fp16" and model.region == request.origin_region
  priority: 1000
```

alex: I'm going to apply that patch now as a canary for the AcmePay route only. Will monitor errors and latency.

(3 minutes later)

alex: applied canary to route /acme/* in eu-west-1. Errors dropped for the canary traffic immediately. :white_check_mark:

maria: rolling the patch to all tool_call traffic in eu-west-1. Sam, can you also open a temp capacity window for fp16 in eu-west-1? If not, we should keep the policy in place until autoscaling stabilizes.
sam: requesting burst capacity from infra; ETA ~6 minutes. Manual override granted for small burst.
jordan: I'll throttle the internal batch job consuming reserved pool to free capacity. Pushing a limited throttle now.

(10 minutes later)

maria: AcmePay confirms improved behavior. Support says error rate back to baseline, latency reduced. Leah, confirm closure message to the customer after we finish triage.
leah: will send update. Draft: "We've mitigated the routing issue by pinning tool_call traffic to fp16 variants in eu-west-1 while we fix the model compatibility matrix." Will send after postmortem updates.

sam: root cause notes so far: model metadata (compatibility matrix) incorrectly advertised tool_call support for quantized variants in eu-west-1, and smart-routing policy had a low-priority rule that allowed quant variants to be considered for tool_call requests. Combined with temporary fp16 capacity exhaustion -> fallback loop.

maria: follow-ups:
- immediate: leave tool_call->fp16 rule until compatibility matrix corrected or quant variants add tool_call support (tracked change request)
- short term: add a pre-routing capability filter to reject candidate variants that do not declare required features (tool_call, context_len > request) — fail open to forcing fallback only once.
- medium term: add telemetry and alerting when fallback count per-request > 1 within 5s (detect loops)

alex: handing off to maria for postmortem and long-term fixes. I'm available for follow-up.
maria: taking incident lead. I'll schedule a postmortem ticket and include: exact time window, affected customers, config diffs, patch applied, telemetry graphs, and remediation plan. Assigning owners: compatibility metadata fix -> sam, routing pre-filter -> eng-runtime (maria), autoscaler tuning -> infra (jordan).
support-bot: Incident severity: S2 (customer-impacting, mitigated). Incident duration: start=2117008245, mitigated=2117008560.

maria: quick repro steps for triage team:
1) craft a request with features: ["tool_call"] and send to eu-west-1 route
2) observe candidate list includes redwood-7b-quant in metadata
3) runtime rejects -> fallback loop if fp16 capacity=0

maria: I'll open the issue in the tracker with config diffs and logs. Closing slack thread once postmortem created. Thanks everyone for fast responses. :pray:

alex: ack, thanks team. Good catch on the metadata drift.

support-bot: ACTIONS:
- sam -> compat-matrix correction ticket #INC-4521
- maria -> postmortem doc + routing pre-filter PR
- jordan -> autoscaler rules + batch throttle policy
- leah -> customer comms sent

support-bot: mark incident resolved in Slack; follow-ups tracked in INC-4521."
